translation: Bodiless, dwelling in bodies, intent on the worship of Kālī.
Resembling the state of one's own reflexive awareness — (the rest of the verse is lacunose in the source).
Of the form of space, named the Endless, bearing the eight forms — Śivā.

sanskrit: pretatve saṃsthitā nityaṃ tasyā devyāstu sarvataḥ ||1/ 5 ||
translation: She abides forever in the state of a corpse; of that Goddess — may it be so everywhere.

sanskrit: abravīt tu  samāsena bhairavo bhairavīṃ  tataḥ ||1/ 7 ||
namo'stu te mahāraudri  saumyarūpe namo'stu te ||1/ 11 ||
tālusthe tu mahākāli  sarvabhakṣye  namo'stu te ||1/ 20 ||
brahmadvāre  sthite  kāli vasturūpe  namo'stu te ||1/ 21 ||
trilakṣānte alakṣasthe nirlakṣe  ca namo'stu te ||1/ 24 ||
sākāre tu nirākāre sarvākāre namo'stu te ||1/ 27 ||
kiṃ vā prayojanaṃ te vai kiṃ vā praśnasya kāraṇam ||1/ 33 ||
kiṃ vā svabhāvabhāvena pṛcchase tu mahāmate ||1/ 34 ||
vadāmyasaṃśayaṃ  tubhyaṃ pṛcchase tu yathā mama ||1/35 ||
aṣṭa  pīṭhāstu ye proktāḥ sarvapīṭheṣu cottamāḥ  ||1/ 39 ||
mānuṣaiśca yathā tathyaṃ aśakyaṃ (?) tu kapāladhṛk ||1/ 48 ||
kālāntare tu saṃprāpte vakṣyāmi tu yathā tathyam  ||1/ 53 ||
tataḥ kālāntare ramye  aśarīrā tviyaṃ  parā ||1/ 61 ||
mahābhairavamekaṃ tu samurcchaṃ  tiṣṭhate tu yat  ||1/ 66 ||
tatastu paramaṃ tattvaṃ prāptaṃ tu paramaṃ śivam  ||1/ 67 ||
tatastu  paramaṃ praśnaṃ  kathayasva tu hṛdgatam ||2/2 ||
avākyaṃ  tat  rahasyaṃ  vai dṛṣṭaṃ sthānavaraṃ  param ||2/3 ||
vadasva paramaṃ jñānaṃ  yat  sthitaṃ me hṛdantare  ||2/7 ||
vakṣyāmi te yathā tathyaṃ  atyantagahanaṃ  śubham ||2/9 ||
tena jñānena vai samyak yoginī yogabhāvagā ||2/12 ||
khecakre tu  yathā labdhā svarūpasthā nirāmayā ||2/18 ||
prāptā tu paramā devyā mahāsiddhipradāstu tāḥ  ||2/19 ||
kathitāstu samāsena khecakre tu yathā matāḥ  ||2/22 ||
tāsāṃ jñānaṃ yathā mantro  melāpaṃ tu mahāmate ||2/23 ||
ṣoḍaśānāṃ tu yad  jñeyaṃ jñānarūpaṃ parāparam ||2/26 ||

translation: Homage to her whose majesty begins with māyā, to her who unfolds the universe — protect me!

sanskrit: abravīt tu  samāsena bhairavo bhairavīṃ  tataḥ ||1/ 7 ||
translation: Homage be to you, O great Raudrī! O gentle-formed one, homage be to you!
O Bhairava's mistress, you who abide in the own-nature whose very form is Will — homage be to you!
O you whose form is Action, O great-formed one, O all-formed one — homage be to you!
O you who are the end of the cessation of being and non-being, O all-absence — homage be to you!

sanskrit: namo'stu te mahāraudri  saumyarūpe namo'stu te ||1/ 11 ||
translation: O you whose interior is the level of bliss, and O you whose form is pervasion — homage be to you!
O Nāda-formed one, O great Nāda — homage be to you, homage to Sadākhyā!
O Śakti-formed one, O body-dwelling one, O all-state-abiding one — homage be [to you]! ('te' absent in the transmitted line)
O you whose form is Śiva, O great Peace, O you beyond peace — homage be to you!
O you dwelling in the interior of the heart-lotus pericarp, O flame-formed one — homage be to you!
O great Kālī dwelling in the palate, O devourer of everything — homage be to you!
O Kālī standing at the gate of Brahmā, O you whose form is the Real — homage be to you!
O you gone to the kanda-station, ever named Kuṇḍalī — homage be to you!
O Kālī, devoid of the six cakras, O mistress of the cakra's end — homage be to you!

sanskrit: tālusthe tu mahākāli  sarvabhakṣye  namo'stu te ||1/ 20 ||
translation: O you at the end of the three marks, O you standing in the unmarked, O markless one — and homage be to you!

sanskrit: brahmadvāre  sthite  kāli vasturūpe  namo'stu te ||1/ 21 ||
translation: O you beyond the level of fragmented form, O mistress of the end of form — homage be to you!
O you with form, O you without form, O you of all forms — homage be to you!
Having made this verse of praise, she then spoke this speech.

sanskrit: trilakṣānte alakṣasthe nirlakṣe  ca namo'stu te ||1/ 24 ||
translation: Why have all the sixty-four mighty ones come?
Bound to the worship of you, the great lords of yoga, eager —

sanskrit: sākāre tu nirākāre sarvākāre namo'stu te ||1/ 27 ||
translation: Devoted to serving you, their faces exceedingly joyful —
By this grace, O Goddess, tell me, O supreme Mistress!
What indeed is your purpose? Or what is the cause of the question?
Or is it by the state of your own nature that you ask, O great-minded one?
I speak to you without doubt; indeed you ask as is mine [to answer].
The supreme one goes before the Goddess; she is capable of effecting dissolution.

sanskrit: kiṃ vā prayojanaṃ te vai kiṃ vā praśnasya kāraṇam ||1/ 33 ||
translation: Even so, the question lies in their hearts, O great lord!

sanskrit: kiṃ vā svabhāvabhāvena pṛcchase tu mahāmate ||1/ 34 ||
translation: Tell me this, O Vāmā(?), according to the rule, in due order.

sanskrit: vadāmyasaṃśayaṃ  tubhyaṃ pṛcchase tu yathā mama ||1/35 ||
translation: The eight seats that have been proclaimed are the best of all seats.
Divine ones, possessed of eight-times-eight (sixty-four) qualities, eager for the worship of own-nature.
Indeed, O Rudra, they are engaged in the great yogas, according to the rule.
It perishes by the supreme reality, as grass cast into fire.

sanskrit: aṣṭa  pīṭhāstu ye proktāḥ sarvapīṭheṣu cottamāḥ  ||1/ 39 ||
translation: The question lying in the heart, unknown to them — in truth.
This best of questions, O Rudra, is unspeakable among all creatures.
Extremely profound, hidden, concealed, more concealed, supreme.
[Unknowable] by gandharvas, by divine kinnaras, by sādhyas and vasus alike.
Even Sadāśiva and Bhairava, and likewise the serpents and the foremost serpents [cannot know it].
And by humans — as is truly [the case] — it is impossible; indeed [for] the skull-bearer (?)
Hard to know, hard to worship, in every way, among all creatures.
In all that has been uttered it is unattainable, indeed; and it is excluded from all states.
Among all beings, O knower of reality, it is not to be revealed — [it is] incomparable.

sanskrit: mānuṣaiśca yathā tathyaṃ aśakyaṃ (?) tu kapāladhṛk ||1/ 48 ||
translation: Today I will tell you [that which] effects the dissolution of all.
When another time has arrived, I will tell [it] truly, as [it is] true.
Grant grace fully, in truth, O impassioned one, for the essential point!
Make manifest, O Śaṅkarī, [that which] abides in the Yoginīs' heart!
Freed from abodes and dwellings, and likewise from lunar mansions and planets.

sanskrit: kālāntare tu saṃprāpte vakṣyāmi tu yathā tathyam  ||1/ 53 ||
translation: Freed, always, from unbroken grains and sesame, and from the fire-rite.
[Freed] by recaka, puraka, and kumbhaka alike — especially.
Freed from saṃyama and niyama alike — great, in reality.
Having spoken this speech, intent on the worship of the Goddess —
Then, at another pleasant time, this supreme one became bodiless.
And having heard this speech, [which passed] from the bodiless one to the embodied one —
Then indeed, O mistress of the god of gods, going into the interior of the level of own-nature —
She set forth with the great yogas, she who is accompanied by the sixty-four.

sanskrit: tataḥ kālāntare ramye  aśarīrā tviyaṃ  parā ||1/ 61 ||
translation: And this was done by the Goddess of gods, according to the rule, for the Yoginīs.
The one great Bhairava who stands absorbed —
Then indeed the supreme principle is attained — the supreme Śiva.
And the sixty-four Yoginīs, proud of the level of the great meaning —
The first chapter.

sanskrit: mahābhairavamekaṃ tu samurcchaṃ  tiṣṭhate tu yat  ||1/ 66 ||
translation: Arise! — of Bhairava, the absorbed one — with the boons of the bearers (text uncertain).

sanskrit: tatastu paramaṃ tattvaṃ prāptaṃ tu paramaṃ śivam  ||1/ 67 ||
translation: Then indeed tell the supreme question that lies in the heart!
That secret is unspeakable; indeed [I have] seen the supreme best abode.
Surrounded by khatvāṅga-staves, by [attendants] beginning with Mahākāla, and by skulls.
I have seen, O Goddess, the wondrous [one] that effects the dissolution of all.

sanskrit: tatastu  paramaṃ praśnaṃ  kathayasva tu hṛdgatam ||2/2 ||
translation: And the sixty-four — principle-formed ones of the Goddess, wholly devoted —

sanskrit: avākyaṃ  tat  rahasyaṃ  vai dṛṣṭaṃ sthānavaraṃ  param ||2/3 ||
translation: Tell the supreme gnosis that stands in the interior of my heart!
Everywhere [it is] the best, to be known, and devoid of all supports.
I will tell you, as [it is] true, the extremely profound auspicious [teaching].
And all beings, all of them, are devoured in that great battle.

sanskrit: vadasva paramaṃ jñānaṃ  yat  sthitaṃ me hṛdantare  ||2/7 ||
translation: From them, directly, springs forth the supreme Kaulika gnosis.
By that gnosis, indeed, the Yoginī goes rightly into the yogic state.

sanskrit: vakṣyāmi te yathā tathyaṃ  atyantagahanaṃ  śubham ||2/9 ||
translation: With the supreme mouth, which dissolves everything.
Bearing the form of Bhairava, they are known as sky-going, gone into the sky.
The Bhairavīs, of terrible bodies, stand in a self-nature devoid of self-nature.

sanskrit: tena jñānena vai samyak yoginī yogabhāvagā ||2/12 ||
translation: Tell that in brief, according to the rule, in due order.
Hear that in brief: the auspicious [truth], more essential than the essential.
As she is obtained in the khecakra, abiding in her own form, free from affliction.
Then the supreme Goddess is attained; and those [yoginīs] are givers of great siddhis.
Radiant on all sides with a mass of great rays.
The mantra-perfected ones are twenty-four; twelve are known in the melāpa.

sanskrit: khecakre tu  yathā labdhā svarūpasthā nirāmayā ||2/18 ||
translation: And they have been told in brief, as they are known in the khecakra.

sanskrit: prāptā tu paramā devyā mahāsiddhipradāstu tāḥ  ||2/19 ||
translation: Their gnosis — as the mantra — is the melāpa, O great-minded one.
By each one's own form [they possess] sovereignty over the void, in all states.
Out of affection for you I will tell [it] in detail, according to the rule.

sanskrit: kathitāstu samāsena khecakre tu yathā matāḥ  ||2/22 ||
translation: And what is to be known of the sixteen — that which is knowledge-formed, supreme and non-supreme.

sanskrit: tāsāṃ jñānaṃ yathā mantro  melāpaṃ tu mahāmate ||2/23 ||
translation: Sūtakī, Mṛtakā, O god, and Madhyāntānāmamadhyataḥ (?)
Haṭharāvā, Arāvasthā, Haṭhabhakṣakī — with a roar.
Antāntā, and Antakāntā, and with the Antakas, Antadāyinī.

sanskrit: ṣoḍaśānāṃ tu yad  jñeyaṃ jñānarūpaṃ parāparam ||2/26 ||
translation: Ālīḍhā and Nirālīḍhā, together with the Sālīḍhālīḍhakas.
Ratnākārā, Ratnagarbhā, Ratnakāntarabhāsakā.
By the sixth part — ending in six spokes — tātītā, śiśivaṃ, shaken (text corrupt).
The Goddess, entered into the seven wombs, established as seven-times-seven-and-one.
